timeline.title: Defense in Lindsay Clancy Case Argues Postpartum Psychosis Affected Her Actions
timeline.summary: In the trial of Lindsay Clancy, her defense has concluded, asserting that she should not be held criminally responsible for the deaths of her children due to postpartum psychosis. The defense highlighted the impact of this rare mental illness, which can cause severe symptoms following childbirth, including command hallucinations. A forensic psychiatrist testified about these effects during the proceedings.
key_facts: Lindsay Clancy's defense rests after presenting testimony on postpartum psychosis.
The defense does not dispute that Clancy killed her children.
Postpartum psychosis is linked to stress, sleep deprivation, and hormonal changes after childbirth.

timeline.title: Lindsay Clancy's Trial Centers on Postpartum Psychosis Defense
timeline.summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense acknowledges that she killed her three children in 2023 but argues she was not criminally responsible due to postpartum psychosis. This rare mental health condition can impair a new mother's perception of reality. A forensic psychiatrist testified in court about the impact of this condition on Clancy's actions.
key_facts: Lindsay Clancy killed her three children in 2023.
The defense claims she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.
A forensic psychiatrist testified about the effects of postpartum psychosis.

timeline.title: Judge Denies Mistrial Request in Lindsay Clancy Trial
timeline.summary: In the ongoing trial of Lindsay Clancy, Judge William Sullivan denied a defense request for a mistrial after a witness mentioned religious themes during testimony. This incident marked the second time a reference to 'mortal sin' arose in court, prompting the defense's unsuccessful call for a mistrial.
key_facts: Judge William Sullivan denied a mistrial request.
The mistrial request was prompted by a witness mentioning religion.
This was the second occurrence of 'mortal sin' being referenced during the trial.
